metadata.source: RBI Financial Markets Regulation Department, SEBI, FIMMDA

money_market.tenor: Short-term debt instruments (Maturity up to 1 year)
money_market.primary_objective: Managing short-term liquidity requirements of banks, corporates, and governments

capital_market.regulator: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
capital_market.tenor: Medium and Long-term capital instruments (Maturity > 1 year)
capital_market.primary_objective: Capital mobilization for corporate expansion, infrastructure, and wealth creation

money_market_instruments.name: Call Money, Notice Money & Term Money
money_market_instruments.nature: Inter-bank uncollateralised borrowing and lending market
money_market_instruments.participants: Scheduled Commercial Banks, Cooperative Banks, Primary Dealers

money_market_instruments.name: Treasury Bills (T-Bills)
money_market_instruments.issuer: Issued by Government of India (managed by RBI)
money_market_instruments.pricing: Issued at a discount to face value and redeemed at par (Face Value). Difference is the yield.
money_market_instruments.eligibility: Individuals, firms, companies, banks, institutions. State Governments do NOT issue T-Bills (they issue State Development Loans - SDLs).

money_market_instruments.name: Cash Management Bills (CMBs)
money_market_instruments.issuer: Government of India in consultation with RBI
money_market_instruments.purpose: To meet temporary mismatches in the cash flow of the Government of India
money_market_instruments.characteristic: Same features as T-Bills but ultra short-term (issued at discount, redeemed at face value)

money_market_instruments.name: Commercial Paper (CP)
money_market_instruments.nature: Unsecured money market promissory note issued by highly rated corporate borrowers, primary dealers (PDs), and all-India financial institutions (AIFIs)
money_market_instruments.minimum_denomination: ₹5 Lakh and multiples of ₹5 Lakh thereafter
money_market_instruments.maturity_period: Minimum 7 days and maximum up to 1 year from the date of issue
money_market_instruments.credit_rating_mandate: Minimum credit rating of A2 as per SEBI approved CRA rating scale

money_market_instruments.name: Certificate of Deposit (CD)
money_market_instruments.nature: Negotiable money market receipt issued by Scheduled Commercial Banks and Select All-India Financial Institutions
money_market_instruments.minimum_denomination: ₹1 Lakh and multiples of ₹1 Lakh thereafter

maturity_period.banks: Minimum 7 days and maximum up to 1 year
maturity_period.financial_institutions: Minimum 1 year and maximum up to 3 years

money_market_instruments.demat: Issued in dematerialised form or as usance promissory note

money_market_instruments.name: Ways and Means Advances (WMA)
money_market_instruments.nature: Temporary loan facility provided by RBI to Central and State Governments to tide over temporary mismatches in receipts and payments

types.description: Clean advance without collateral at prevailing Repo Rate
Extended against the pledge of Government of India securities

money_market_instruments.repayment_period: Clean advances must be fully repaid within 90 days

segments.description: Market for new securities where capital is raised directly from investors by issuers.

modes.description: First time a privately held company sells shares to the public on a stock exchange.
Issuance of additional shares by an already listed company.
Offering new shares to existing shareholders in proportion to their existing holding at a discounted price.
Private placement of shares by listed company exclusively to QIBs (Mutual Funds, FPIs, Insurers).

segments.description: Market where already issued securities are bought and sold among investors.

depositories_in_india.name: Central Depository Services (India) Limited (CDSL)
depositories_in_india.promoters: BSE and leading banks (SBI, BoI, BoB)

specialized_bonds.name: Masala Bonds
specialized_bonds.description: Rupee-denominated debt instruments issued by Indian entities in foreign overseas markets to raise capital, transferring currency risk to foreign investors.

specialized_bonds.name: Sovereign Green Bonds (SGrBs)
specialized_bonds.description: Rupee-denominated sovereign bonds issued by Government of India to raise proceeds exclusively for public sector green and climate-friendly infrastructure projects.

specialized_bonds.name: Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGB)
specialized_bonds.description: Government securities denominated in grams of gold issued by RBI on behalf of GoI, paying 2.50% annual fixed interest with 8-year tenor.

exam_traps.trap: Believing State Governments can issue Treasury Bills (T-Bills).
exam_traps.fact: State Governments CANNOT issue T-Bills. T-Bills are issued solely by the Central Government. State Governments issue State Development Loans (SDLs).

exam_traps.trap: Confusing the minimum denomination of Commercial Paper (CP) with Certificate of Deposit (CD).
exam_traps.fact: Commercial Paper (CP) minimum is ₹5 Lakh. Certificate of Deposit (CD) minimum is ₹1 Lakh.

exam_traps.trap: Thinking Notice Money is for up to 30 days.
exam_traps.fact: Notice Money is strictly 2 to 14 days. Term Money is 15 to 365 days.

exam_traps.trap: Assuming Capital Market is regulated by RBI.
exam_traps.fact: Money Market is regulated by RBI. Capital Market is regulated by SEBI.
